questions.question: In blood relation reasoning, what does the term 'nephew' mean?
options: Son of a sibling
Daughter of a sibling
Brother of a parent
Child of an uncle or aunt
questions.rationale: Nephew is the son of one's sibling, as distinct from niece (daughter of a sibling).

questions.question: What is a 'cousin' in blood relation terms?
options: Sibling of a parent
Child of an uncle or aunt
Spouse of a sibling
Parent of a grandparent
questions.rationale: A cousin is the child of an uncle or aunt — someone from the same generation but a different immediate family branch.

questions.question: Why should generation, gender, marriage, and parent-child/sibling links be tracked separately when modeling a family?
options: It isn't necessary — one combined label is enough
Because keeping them separate prevents confusing similar-sounding relations and supports accurate step-by-step reasoning
Because exams only ask about gender
Because parent-child links are the only ones that matter
questions.rationale: Tracking these dimensions separately, rather than one vague label, is what lets you reason step by step without conflating relations that sound similar but differ in gender, generation, or link type.

questions.question: What is the key rule about gender and relation being different?
options: Gender and relation are always the same thing
A relation term can imply gender (like 'brother'), but the underlying link (sibling) is what actually matters for tracing family structure
Gender never matters in blood relation puzzles
Relation terms never specify gender
questions.rationale: Terms like brother/sister both describe the same underlying sibling link with different genders attached — the structural link matters for tracing relationships, with gender as an additional attribute.

questions.question: How is a family graph typically represented?
options: As a single flat list of names
As a graph where each person is a node and each relationship is an edge
As a table of random numbers
Family graphs cannot be represented visually
questions.rationale: A family tree is a graph: each node represents a person, and each edge represents a relationship (parent-child, sibling, or spouse) connecting them.

questions.question: What defines a sibling relationship?
options: Two people who share at least one parent
Two people who are married
Two people from different generations
Two people with the same surname
questions.rationale: Siblings are people who share at least one parent — the sibling link connects people at the same generation under a common parent.

questions.question: What is the relationship between an uncle and their nephew's parent?
options: No relation at all
The uncle is a sibling of the nephew's parent
The uncle is the nephew's grandparent
The uncle is the nephew's cousin
questions.rationale: An uncle is defined as the brother of a parent — so the uncle and the nephew's parent are siblings of each other.

questions.question: In blood relation problems, what is a 'direct' relation as opposed to an 'indirect' one?
options: Direct relations involve marriage only
A direct relation is a single-step link (like parent-child or sibling); an indirect relation is derived by chaining multiple direct links together
There is no difference between the two
Indirect relations are always incorrect
questions.rationale: Direct relations are single links (parent-child, sibling, spouse), while indirect relations (like 'uncle' or 'cousin') are composed by chaining two or more direct links together.

questions.question: If P is the father of Q, and Q is the father of R, what generation gap exists between P and R?
options: Same generation
One generation apart
Two generations apart
Cannot be determined
questions.rationale: P is Q's parent (one generation up) and Q is R's parent (another generation up), so P is R's grandparent — two generations apart.

questions.question: Which of these terms is generation-neutral (doesn't by itself tell you the generation gap)?
options: Grandfather
Father
Cousin
Grandmother
questions.rationale: 'Cousin' describes someone in the same generation as you but says nothing by itself about direct generational distance the way 'father' or 'grandfather' do — its generation is inferred from the underlying parent-child chain.
